links.comparator_used: Standard of care (control arm, no behavioral nudges) among patients flagged high-risk by the ML mortality algorithm
links.outcome: Mean daily end-of-life spending in the last 6 months of life
links.effect: $377.96 vs $449.92 unadjusted; adjusted mean difference -$75.33 (95% CI -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02); $13,747 adjusted savings per decedent; lower systemic therapy (-$44.59), office/outpatient (-$9.62) and other therapy (-$8.65) spending; no difference in acute care, long-term care or hospice spending
links.quote: The intervention was associated with lower unadjusted mean daily spending in the last 6 months of life for the intervention group versus controls ($377.96 vs. $449.92; adjusted mean difference, -$75.33; 95% confidence interval, -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02), translating to $13,747 total adjusted savings per decedent and $13 million in cumulative savings across all decedents in the intervention group.

design_hint: ML mortality-risk prediction with behavioral nudges to clinicians prompting serious illness conversations
